summary: Iteration 2 focused on verifying (a) real training threshold -0.05246478086634679 loaded into ML scorer and (b) /api/admin/demo/attack now dual-fires rule + ML logs with rich ml_verdict payload, plus (c) frontend SecurityDemo panel renders both RULE and ML badges inline. Result: 12/12 new backend tests PASS. Frontend Playwright verified admin login → Security Demo tab → SQL Injection & Brute Force triggers produce inline dual verdicts (RULE + ML with predicted class, confidence, anomaly, threshold), and Attack Feed shows both rule and ML rows for the same simulated IP (68 RULE + 32 ML badges visible).

minor.issue: ml_verdict returns anomaly_threshold rounded to 4 decimals (-0.0525) instead of full-precision -0.05246478086634679 requested by spec. Cause: /app/backend/ml/ids_inference.py line 90 does `round(_ANOMALY_THRESHOLD, 4)`. Underlying model_card.json holds correct full-precision value; only the API/UI display is rounded. Cosmetic. Fix: remove or widen the round() call if full precision is required in ml_verdict payload.

action_items: OPTIONAL: If spec strictly requires full-precision anomaly_threshold in ml_verdict, drop the `round(_ANOMALY_THRESHOLD, 4)` in /app/backend/ml/ids_inference.py:90 (frontend displays it via .toFixed(3) so precision loss is only in the raw API JSON).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 807 lines — crossing the 700-line threshold; consider splitting admin routes into a separate module.
sklearn 1.8→1.9 unpickle warnings are cosmetic (documented in review request) — safe to ignore for now but plan a re-pickle in current sklearn version to eliminate warnings and future breakage.
admin_demo_attack correctly excludes _id (calls .pop('_id', None) on both logs) — good.
Middleware skip_ml for authenticated admins on /api/admin/* prevents dashboard-polling noise — correct decision.
ML scorer wrapped in try/except and only warns — good defensive coding so a ML failure never blocks the demo endpoint.
seed_data_creation: None. Test-created attack_logs entries share ephemeral simulated IPs and are cleaned by demo helper; blocked_ips test cleans its own inserted IP.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Threshold now correctly loaded from model_card.json (verified value -0.05246478086634679). ml_verdict fields returned in API response are all rounded to 4 decimals by ids_inference.py — tests use pytest.approx(abs=1e-4) for the threshold comparison. Predicted labels for each demo kind matched exactly (sql_injection→sql_injection, brute_force→brute_force_login, bot_flood→bot_flood, unauthorized_admin→unauthorized_admin, malicious_upload→malicious_upload, xss→xss_attempt). Frontend inline verdict renders correctly with data-testids ad-demo-verdicts-{kind}, ad-demo-ml-action-{kind}, ad-demo-ml-predicted-{kind}, ad-demo-ml-conf-{kind}, ad-demo-ml-anom-{kind}. Attack Feed SourceBadge renders both RULE and ML consistently.
rca of the issue: No functional bugs. Minor cosmetic: ml_verdict.anomaly_threshold in API response is rounded to 4 decimals because /app/backend/ml/ids_inference.py line 90 calls round(_ANOMALY_THRESHOLD, 4). The full-precision value is still loaded from model_card.json (line 53) and used for the actual anomaly comparison — this is display-only rounding.
